# READ-ch12s — Phase R2, main volume §12.11.1 "The axes, and what each one sees", third segment: the dichotomy under enlargement, the tenth's battery, the order of K and J, what the twelfth and thirteenth axes measure (chat 76)

Member The_Method_1_6-2.md (BUILD90 main, md5 4aef772b…), L3136–L3176 (41 lines, none over 400 characters; §12.11.1.1 opens at L3177), read in full against the referee table (L3130–3134, every entry reproduced by r2-ch12r), §12.11.4 (L3457–3460), §12.11.3 (L3394), the Register (240 at R L947–949; 241 at R L951–953; 1790), exclusion (iii) at L6909–6912, §7.4 (L1789), READ-ch12q (12q-01, 12q-04, 12q-05) and READ-ch12r (12r-01), tower-2.py (c0bce27a…) and the segment instrument r2-ch12s.py (r2lib by path; terms/new_terms and L8_at/phi_at/TERMS lifted verbatim from r2-ch12q.py and r2-ch12r.py; every cell of Λ₁₁, Λ₁₂ and Λ₁₃, every Λ₈ cell of the four density caps, and the exact ninth and tenth objects in full). Pointers: §12.11.1 (L3141, a self-pointer — see 12s-02), Register 240 (L3144), §7.4 (L3147), §12.11.4 (L3154) resolve to headings; Register 241 (L3144) resolves; "exclusion (iii)" (L3171) resolves to L6909–6912 (`Systems without interior cells … the levels are 40–50% configuration-mixed with no assignable parent`). No lowercase `register NNN` in range. Census rows in range: none (CENSUS-CLOSURES-ch12s.tsv is a header).

## A. Deviations (both texts)

**12s-01 · subject matter.** L3137–3139: `Every density except the thirteenth **falls** as the object grows, so the envelope gap widens with scale — the price of certainty is not a constant but an increasing function of the index's size`. MEASURED on the table the section prints (L3130–3134; all 24 entries reproduced in READ-ch12r): axes 9, 9′, 10 and 11 fall strictly and 13 rises strictly, but axis 12 goes **31.4 → 36.7 → 28.2 → 22.4** — up 5.3 points at the first enlargement (s, p at k ≤ 6), then down. "Every density except the thirteenth" is five of six on the first step; the widening-with-scale reading holds for the counting axes and axis 11, not for axis 12 across the sweep. 12r-01's corrected axis-10 column (44.7 / 31.9 / 26.0 / 22.9) still falls.

**12s-02 · pointer to a claim that has no site.** L3140–3143: `converging on the ⅔ that §12.11.1 states as its nominal value. The gap between ⅔ and the measured figure was attributed there to the K = 0 singlet`. Register 241: `TOWARD THE ⅔ §12.11.1 STATES AS NOMINAL`. MEASURED (grep of the main member): ⅔ occurs once in the volume — at L3141 — and "K = 0 singlet" twice (L3142, L3168); §12.11.1 states no nominal value for the thirteenth axis and makes no attribution before this sentence. The claim itself is right (B: density₁₃ = (2N − N₀)/(3N − N₀), the K = 0 share falls 19.2 → 18.3 → 8.7 → 5.2 %, the limit is ⅔), but "there" points nowhere on the live text; Register 241 carries the same pointer.

**12s-03 · undefined term and notation.** L3146–3148: `**And two facts of the tenth's battery worth the print.** Its 10-box appears at caps (5,5,2,6) and not at the book's — the known small-cap effect, caught by §7.4's own discipline, as it caught the same absence for Λ₈ and Λ₉`. "10-box" has this one site in the six volumes; no N-box is defined anywhere (the only sense of "box" in Chapter 8 is the bounding box, L1934), "the tenth's battery" names no test, and the cap tuple (5,5,2,6) is four-valued where L1800 and L3121 write five. Unverifiable as written; nothing measured for or against it.

**12s-04 · internal contradiction, and a triangle that is not the printed tower's.** L3152–3153: `K precedes J: K's parents are J_c and f`; L3065–3066 (S1): `the bound 2K ≤ 2J_c + 2f_max has one parent`. The section reads K with two parents here and one there — 12q-04's tension (Register 1790 against L3066), now inside §12.11.1. L3154–3156: `carrying both with all admissible bounds closes the 11–12–13 cycle in the constraint graph — a triangle in both senses at once`. MEASURED: under the table's bounds K has the parent J_c only and J the parent K only, so 11–12–13 is a path (READ-ch12q B: 13 edges, one triangle 2S′–g–v); the implied 2J ≤ 2J_c + 2f_max + 1 holds on every cell of Λ₁₃, but the converse 2J_c ≤ 2J + 2f_max + 1 fails on **10,370 of 199,130** cells — "all admissible bounds" names an object smaller than Λ₁₃, and the 11–12–13 triangle belongs to it, not to the tower whose 199,130 cells the section prints.

## B. Verified (all MEASURED unless marked; r2-ch12s.py)

- L3140 the thirteenth rises 64.4 → 64.5 → 65.7 → 66.1 (record-carried from r2-ch12r) and the mechanism L3141–3143 describes reproduces exactly: with N₀ the K = 0 cells of Λ₁₂, density₁₃ = (2N − N₀)/(3N − N₀) = 64.4 / 64.5 / 65.7 / 66.1 % at the four caps (Λ₁₂ = 70,905 / 1,238,877 / 102,179,658 / 1,370,242,656; K = 0 share 19.2 / 18.3 / 8.7 / 5.2 %), and 66.7 % with no K = 0 cell. Registers 240 and 241 resolve.
- L3148–3150 `the obstruction … moves up one level, onto v itself — v ≡ g mod 2 and the conjugation ceiling, both still outside the language`: the exact ninth object (Λ₈ × realised spins, 1,054 cells) is not pairwise-closed (101,184 join and 101,184 meet failures on 1,110,916 ordered pairs; ℛ adds 491 cells) and the exact tenth (× realised seniorities, 1,132 cells) is not either (144,832 / 144,832; ℛ adds 1,060). The two conditions named here are exactly 12q-01 (parity) and 12r-01 (the ceiling v ≤ 4f+2−g): the section knows them as obstructions at L3149 and omits them from the density definition at L3080–3082.
- L3152–3154 / §12.11.4 (L3458–3460, verified here because L3153 rests on it): the J-set of a channel is the same through K and direct (J_c ⊗ (ℓ ⊗ s), j = f ± ½) in 12 of 12 (2J_c, f) pairs; the J-fibre density is 64.4 % through K (axis 13 over Λ₁₂) and **39.4 %** direct (33,325 realised of 84,490 allowed by 2J ≤ 2J_c + 2f_max + 1 over Λ₁₁; the two-sided |2J − 2J_c| ≤ 2f_max + 1 would give 41.7 %); `25 points` = 25.0. `axis 13 is reachable from axis 11 without axis 12` — the direct set exists at every channel.
- L3158–3159 every f = 0 channel of Λ₁₁ (7,575 cells) has the singleton K-set {2J_c}; L3167–3168 the J-fibre is a doublet at K > 0 (57,320 cells of Λ₁₂) and a singleton at K = 0 (13,585). L3174 `up to one parity point`: the bound |2J − 2K| ≤ 1 admits three values of which coupling realises two — the third is the parity-wrong 2J = 2K.
- L3136–3137 `the counting axes stay exact and all three coupling axes stay envelopes, at the d shell and at the f` restates §12.11.3's classification (Register 240) at the referee caps; the densities themselves are READ-ch12r B. The classification is §12.11.3.1's segment (DEFERRED 12j-01, "three values, not two").
- L3171 `configurations at 40–50% in the book's own exclusion (iii)` resolves to L6912's figure.

## C. Incidental

- L3139 `which no part of this book had predicted` and L3143 `a route the book did not have when it made it` are narrative about the book's history; not testable.
- L3152 `The order matters and is not the order first written down` — the earlier order is not stated; the K-before-J cost is §12.11.4's 25 points (B).
- L3160–3165 (what K measures; when it is a good quantum number) and L3169–3175 (`the only coordinate in the entire tower that nature conserves exactly … by rotational invariance`; `The two ends of the tower trade places`) are physical interpretation, marked as such by their own wording; nothing in them is a tower computation.
- With §12.11.1 read in full (L3032–3176, three segments), the DEFERRED items assigned to it are all closed (READ-ch12q: the tower amendment and the 2S′ ≤ g edge, the Figure 12.4 caption against Register 1790, L3067's 3.5 %); the section's own figures reproduce except the three named in 12q-02, 12r-01 and 12s-01, and its definitions omit the two conditions it names at L3149.

# r2-ch12s.py — Phase R2, main §12.11.1 third segment (L3136–3176), chat 76.

#     singleton {2J_c}; L3167–3168 the J doublet except at K = 0. (5) L3148–3150 the exact ninth and tenth objects (realised
#     spins only; realised seniorities only, with v ≡ g mod 2 and v ≤ 4f+2−g) — closure by pairwise joins/meets and by ℛ's box
#     sweep: is the obstruction outside the language. (6) L3152–3156 the J_c–J pair under the table's bounds (no direct edge;
#     the would-be admissible bound 2J_c ≤ 2J + 2f_max + 1 counted against every cell of Λ₁₃).
# terms/new_terms lifted verbatim from r2-ch12q.py; L8_at/phi_at/TERMS lifted verbatim from r2-ch12r.py (chat 76) — owed to r2lib. Deterministic.
import importlib.util, os, itertools
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
import numpy as np
H = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
s = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('r2lib', os.path.join(H, 'r2lib.py')); r2lib = importlib.util.module_from_spec(s); s.loader.exec_module(r2lib); T = r2lib.load_tower()
PHI, FMAX = T.PHI, T.FMAX

# lifted verbatim from r2-ch12q.py (chat 76)
def terms(l, k):
    if k == 0: return Counter({(0, 0): 1})
    orbs = [(ml, ms) for ml in range(-l, l + 1) for ms in (-1, 1)]
    ms_count = Counter((2 * sum(o[0] for o in c), sum(o[1] for o in c)) for c in itertools.combinations(orbs, k))
    out = Counter()
    while ms_count:
        ML2 = max(m for m, _ in ms_count); MS2 = max(sv for m, sv in ms_count if m == ML2)
        out[(MS2, ML2)] += 1
        for ml2 in range(-ML2, ML2 + 1, 2):
            for ms2 in range(-MS2, MS2 + 1, 2):
                ms_count[(ml2, ms2)] -= 1
                if ms_count[(ml2, ms2)] == 0: del ms_count[(ml2, ms2)]
                assert ms_count.get((ml2, ms2), 0) >= 0
    return out
# lifted verbatim from r2-ch12q.py (chat 76)
def new_terms(l, v): return terms(l, v) - terms(l, v - 2) if v >= 2 else terms(l, v)   # multiset difference (L3081)
# lifted verbatim from r2-ch12r.py (chat 76)
_T = {}
def TERMS(l, k):
    if (l, k) not in _T: _T[(l, k)] = terms(l, k)
    return _T[(l, k)]
# lifted verbatim from r2-ch12r.py (chat 76)
def L8_at(caps):
    n_max, e_max, l_max, k_max, f_max = caps
    return [(n, l, k, q, e, f, g, S2) for n in range(1, n_max + 1) for l in range(0, min(l_max, n - 1) + 1) for k in range(1, min(k_max, 4 * l + 2) + 1)
            for q in range(0, k + 1) for e in range(1, e_max + 1) for f in range(0, min(f_max, e - 1) + 1) for g in range(0, min(4 * f + 2, q) + 1) for S2 in range(0, k + 1)]
# lifted verbatim from r2-ch12r.py (chat 76)
def phi_at(caps):
    n_max, e_max, l_max, k_max, f_max = caps
    raw = {k: max(L2 + s2 for l in range(l_max + 1) if k <= 4 * l + 2 for (s2, L2) in TERMS(l, k)) for k in range(1, k_max + 1)}
    env = {}; run = 0
    for k in range(1, k_max + 1): run = max(run, raw[k]); env[k] = run
    return raw, env

# ---- (1) monotonicity over the referee table (L3130–3134; every entry reproduced by r2-ch12r)
CAPS = [(3, 3, 1, 3, 1), (4, 4, 1, 6, 1), (5, 5, 2, 10, 2), (5, 5, 3, 14, 3)]
TAB = {'9': [63.7, 54.2, 49.4, 46.6], '9′': [67.5, 60.3, 55.6, 53.0], '10': [44.7, 33.2, 28.4, 25.9], '11': [17.0, 7.0, 4.9, 4.2], '12': [31.4, 36.7, 28.2, 22.4], '13': [64.4, 64.5, 65.7, 66.1]}
TAB10c = [44.7, 31.9, 26.0, 22.9]   # 12r-01's corrected axis-10 column
fall = {a: all(x > y for x, y in zip(v, v[1:])) for a, v in TAB.items()}; rise = {a: all(x < y for x, y in zip(v, v[1:])) for a, v in TAB.items()}
print(f'== L3137–3140 over the four caps: strictly falling {[a for a in TAB if fall[a]]}, strictly rising {[a for a in TAB if rise[a]]}, neither {[a for a in TAB if not fall[a] and not rise[a]]} — axis 12 goes {TAB["12"]} (up {TAB["12"][1]-TAB["12"][0]:+.1f} at the first enlargement, then down); axis 10 corrected (12r-01) {TAB10c} falling {all(x > y for x, y in zip(TAB10c, TAB10c[1:]))}')

# ---- (2) the thirteenth's rise and the ⅔ limit via the K = 0 share
print('== L3140–3143 density₁₃ = (2N − N₀)/(3N − N₀), N₀ = the K = 0 cells of Λ₁₂:')
for caps, printed in zip(CAPS, TAB['13']):
    raw, env = phi_at(caps); f_max = caps[4]; B10 = lambda g: (g + 1) * (g + 2) // 2
    N = N0 = 0
    for c in L8_at(caps):
        w = B10(c[6]); k = c[2]; N0 += w * (env[k] + 1); N += w * sum(jc + 2 * f_max + 1 for jc in range(env[k] + 1))
    print(f'   {caps}: Λ12 {N:,}, K = 0 cells {N0:,} = {100*N0/N:.1f}% → density₁₃ {100*(2*N-N0)/(3*N-N0):.1f}% (printed {printed}); with no K = 0 cell the value would be {100*2/3:.1f}%')
print('   the nominal ⅔ and its attribution to the K = 0 singlet have no site in §12.11.1 (L3032–3176) or elsewhere in the main member except L3141–3142 itself (grep ⅔, "K = 0 singlet"): record-carried from the read')

# ---- (3) §12.11.4 through L3152–3154: the J-set of a channel through K and direct
L11, L12, L13 = T.L11(), T.L12(), T.L13()
def Jset_viaK(jc2, f2): return sorted({j for K2 in range(abs(jc2 - f2), jc2 + f2 + 1, 2) for j in (K2 - 1, K2 + 1) if j >= 0})
def Jset_direct(jc2, f2): return sorted({j for j2 in ({1} if f2 == 0 else {f2 - 1, f2 + 1}) for j in range(abs(jc2 - j2), jc2 + j2 + 1, 2)})   # J_c ⊗ (ℓ ⊗ s): j = f ± ½
pairs = [(jc2, f) for jc2 in range(0, 6) for f in (0, 1)]
same = sum(1 for jc2, f in pairs if Jset_viaK(jc2, 2 * f) == Jset_direct(jc2, 2 * f))
print(f'== §12.11.4 (L3458–3460) recoupling: the J-set through K equals the direct J-set in {same} of {len(pairs)} (2J_c, f) pairs')
num_d = sum(len(Jset_direct(c[10], 2 * c[5])) for c in L11); den_a = sum(c[10] + 2 * FMAX + 2 for c in L11)
den_b = sum((c[10] + 2 * FMAX + 1) - max(0, c[10] - 2 * FMAX - 1) + 1 for c in L11)
num_K = sum(2 if c[11] >= 1 else 1 for c in L12); den_K = len(L13)
print(f'   J-fibre density through K (axis 13 over Λ12): {num_K:,}/{den_K:,} = {100*num_K/den_K:.1f}% | direct over Λ11, realised {num_d:,}: under the one-sided bound 2J ≤ 2J_c + 2f_max + 1 ({den_a:,} values) {100*num_d/den_a:.1f}%, under the two-sided |2J − 2J_c| ≤ 2f_max + 1 ({den_b:,} values) {100*num_d/den_b:.1f}% | printed 64.4 / 39.4, L3153 "25 points" = {64.4-39.4:.1f}')

# ---- (4) L3158–3159 and L3167–3168
f0 = [c for c in L11 if c[5] == 0]
print(f'== L3158 f = 0 channels of Λ11: {len(f0):,} cells; realised K-set = {{2J_c}} (one value) in all: {all(list(range(abs(c[10]), c[10]+1, 2)) == [c[10]] for c in f0)} | L3167 J-fibre a doublet at K > 0 ({sum(1 for c in L12 if c[11] >= 1):,} cells), a singleton at K = 0 ({sum(1 for c in L12 if c[11] == 0):,})')

# ---- (5) the exact ninth and tenth objects (realised values only) — closure
L8, L9, L10 = T.L8(), T.L9(), T.L10()
spin = {(l, g): sorted({s2 for (s2, _) in TERMS(l, g)}) for l in (0, 1) for g in range(4)}
X9 = [c + (s2,) for c in L8 for s2 in spin[(c[5], c[6])]]
def v_real(f, g, s2p): return [v for v in range(s2p, g + 1) if (g - v) % 2 == 0 and v <= 4 * f + 2 - g and any(x == s2p for (x, _) in new_terms(f, v))]
X10 = [c + (v,) for c in X9 for v in v_real(c[5], c[6], c[8])]
def Rbox(X):
    A = np.array(X, dtype=np.int64); d = A.shape[1]; vals = [np.unique(A[:, i]) for i in range(d)]; phi = {}
    for i in range(d):
        for j in range(d):
            if i == j: continue
            m = np.full(int(A[:, j].max()) + 1, -1, dtype=np.int64)
            for v in vals[j]: m[v] = A[A[:, j] <= v, i].max()
            phi[(i, j)] = m
    G = np.array(np.meshgrid(*vals, indexing='ij')).reshape(d, -1).T; ok = np.ones(len(G), dtype=bool)
    for (i, j), m in phi.items(): ok &= G[:, i] <= m[G[:, j]]
    return int(ok.sum())
for name, X, note in [('Λ9-exact (realised spins only)', X9, 'the parity g mod 2 and the ceiling min(g, 4f+2−g)'), ('Λ10-exact (realised seniorities only)', X10, 'v ≡ g mod 2 and v ≤ 4f+2−g')]:
    nn, jl, ml = r2lib.closure(X); r = Rbox(X)
    print(f'== L3148–3150 {name}: {len(X):,} cells | pairwise closure on {nn:,} ordered pairs: join failures {jl:,}, meet failures {ml:,} | |ℛ(X)| = {r:,} (E = {r-len(X):,}): the exact set is {"" if r == len(X) else "not "}expressible by pairwise bounds — the obstruction is {note}')

Member The_Method_1_6-2.md (BUILD90 main, md5 4aef772b…), L3177–L3204 (28 lines, none over 106 characters; §12.11.1.2 opens at L3205), read in full against §12.11.1 (L3077–3086 the density definition; L3126–3134 the referee table), Appendix F.3 (L11278–11300), §6.2.1 (L1681–1684), the Register (387 at R L1435–1437; 388 at R L1439–1441; 389 at R L1443–1445), READ-ch12q (12q-01) and READ-ch12r (12r-01; the referee table reproduced), tower-2.py (c0bce27a…) and the segment instrument r2-ch12t.py (r2lib by path; terms/new_terms/jc_values and TERMS/L8_at/phi_at lifted verbatim from r2-ch12q.py and r2-ch12r.py; every cell of Λ₁₀ at each of the four caps — 2,535 / 38,299 / 90,955 / 173,554 — with the tower's own Λ₁₀ and Λ₁₁ as the control at the book's caps). Pointers: §12.11.1 (L3178, L3200) resolves to the heading and to L3077–3086 / L3130–3134 — see 12t-02; F.3 (L3179, L3201) resolves to the heading L11278 and not to the claim — see 12t-03; Registers 387, 388 (L3203) resolve (R L1435, L1439); 388 restates the four figures and inherits 12t-01, 12t-02 and 12t-03. ## A. Deviations (both texts)

**12t-01 · subject matter — the fall is attributed to the d shell, which is absent at the row where it happens.** L3194–3195: `It falls from 77.9% to 47.0% when the d shell opens, then rises to 50.3% and 52.5% as the shells widen further.`; L3197–3198: `Opening the d shell admits many k values whose φ̂ is set by the largest term of the widest shell, so the envelope grows faster than the exact set.` L3186 names the tuple (n_max, e_max, ℓ_max, k_max, f_max) and L3190 prints the 47.0 % row at (4, 4, 1, 6, 1): ℓ_max = 1, shells present s and p only (MEASURED, r2-ch12t). The d shell enters at the third row, (4, 4, 2, 6, 2), where the density rises to 50.3 %. MEASURED (r2-ch12t, every Λ₁₀ cell): the fall is k_max 3 → 6 — p⁴, p⁵, p⁶ enter under the running envelope φ̂ = 5 (p³'s ²D) while their own largest 2J_c are 4, 3, 0; the shortfall at that row is 120,188 of 226,609, of which p⁶ 89,250, p⁵ 20,088, p⁴ 5,250, s² 5,040, s¹ 560. Single-cap variation from the book's caps: k_max alone, (3,3,1,6,1), gives 47.1 %; ℓ_max alone, (3,3,2,3,1), gives 57.0 %; adding the d shell to the 47.0 % row, (4,4,2,6,1), gives 50.6 % — a rise, because d¹ … d⁵ cells sit exactly at the envelope. `the envelope grows faster than the exact set` holds for the first step only (×16.68 against ×10.05; the second and third steps are ×5.41 against ×5.80 and ×1.91 against ×1.99). The two mechanisms of L3197–3199 are real but attached to the wrong steps: the fall is the running envelope over k (k_max); the recovery is the d shell (ℓ_max). Register 388 repeats `falling 77.9% to 47.0% as the d shell opens`.

**12t-02 · subject matter — "the eleventh axis's density" names two quantities, and this section says it is §12.11.1's.** L3178–3179: `§12.11.1 reports the coupling axes' densities at the book's caps and does not say what they do when the caps move. **This is that measurement**`; L3200: `§12.11.1's single figure could not show it`. §12.11.1 defines the density (L3077–3079) as the values `exact vector coupling realises` over the values the bound allows, with the core's J at axis 11 `restricted to terms carrying the cell's own multiplicity 2S` (L3082–3083), and prints the eleventh axis at 17.0 (L3084; L3130–3134: 17.0 / 7.0 / 4.9 / 4.2), reproduced by r2-ch12q, r2-ch12r and here (2,310 / 13,585 = 17.0 %; 15,953 / 226,609 = 7.0 % at (4,4,1,6,1)). MEASURED (r2-ch12t): the four printed exact counts 10,585 / 106,421 / 616,725 / 1,228,816 reproduce under exactly one reading of L3183–3185 — for each Λ₁₀ cell, every integer 2J_c from 0 to the largest 2J_c among all terms of ℓᵏ, regardless of the cell's 2S and of parity — so `sum those` sums interval sizes, not the maxima (summing the maxima gives 8,050 / 68,122 / 525,770 / 1,055,262), and the `exact count` includes values no term realises (odd 2J_c at even k, and every value below the maximum whether realised or not; the realised set at the cell's own 2S gives 2,310, the interval to its maximum 4,975, the parity interval 5,855). At the same caps the two definitions give 77.9 against 17.0 and 47.0 against 7.0. Under §12.11.1's own definition the four-cap sequence is 17.0 / 7.0 / 9.2 / 9.7 — also non-monotone, so the finding survives at other values. Neither section names the other's figure. Same class as 12o-01 (one name, two quantities); Registers 388 and 389 carry §12.11.1.1's.

**12t-03 · pointer to F.3 for a standard F.3 does not state.** L3179–3181: `stated to the standard F.3 defines and no number in this book had reached — the method named with its input set, the inputs printed, and the result recomputed under variation rather than once`; L3201: `why the fourth column of F.3 exists`. F.3 as printed (L11278–11300; rebuilt at Register 1780) states the standard as four columns — the method, the input set, the inputs, the refutation (`the test that would kill the claim`, L11289) — and nowhere mentions recomputation under variation (MEASURED: the table's rows and a grep of L11278–11300). The fourth column §12.11.1.1 credits itself with is not F.3's, and the section names no test that would refute its claim. Further sites of the same wording: §6.2.1 L1681–1684 (`F.3's highest standard — the method named with its input set, the inputs printed, and the result recomputed at four proton-number cutoffs`; not recorded in READ-ch6), §22.1.1.1 (L5982) and L9150 (`the three figures recomputed under variation at registers 388, 391 and 392`) — for their segments and Appendix F's; Register 388 (`definition stated with inputs · inputs printed · verification under variation`) and 389 carry the same three-part statement.

## B. Verified (all MEASURED; r2-ch12t.py)

# r2-ch12t.py — Phase R2, main §12.11.1.1 (L3177–3204), chat 77.
# L3183–3192: "for each cell of Λ₁₀, enumerate the terms of the source shell by vector coupling and take the largest 2J_c
# that occurs; sum those over the cells to get the exact count. Divide by |Λ₁₁|, which is the same enumeration with 2J_c
# bounded by φ̂(k) instead" — the four printed rows (caps, |Λ₁₁|, exact, density) re-measured on every Λ₁₀ cell at each
# cap under the method as written and under its candidate readings; L3194–3195 monotonicity; L3197–3199 the causes
# ("when the d shell opens"; "the envelope grows faster than the exact set"); §12.11.1's own axis-11 figure (L3084 17.0 %,
# realised values) at the same caps. terms / new_terms / jc_values lifted verbatim from r2-ch12q.py (chat 76), TERMS / L8_at /
# phi_at verbatim from r2-ch12r.py (chat 76) — all owed to r2lib. tower-2.py by path via r2lib. Deterministic.
import importlib.util, os, itertools, math
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
H = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
s = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('r2lib', os.path.join(H, 'r2lib.py')); r2lib = importlib.util.module_from_spec(s); s.loader.exec_module(r2lib); T = r2lib.load_tower()

# lifted verbatim from r2-ch12q.py (chat 76)
def terms(l, k):
    if k == 0: return Counter({(0, 0): 1})
    orbs = [(ml, ms) for ml in range(-l, l + 1) for ms in (-1, 1)]
    ms_count = Counter((2 * sum(o[0] for o in c), sum(o[1] for o in c)) for c in itertools.combinations(orbs, k))
    out = Counter()
    while ms_count:
        ML2 = max(m for m, _ in ms_count); MS2 = max(sv for m, sv in ms_count if m == ML2)
        out[(MS2, ML2)] += 1
        for ml2 in range(-ML2, ML2 + 1, 2):
            for ms2 in range(-MS2, MS2 + 1, 2):
                ms_count[(ml2, ms2)] -= 1
                if ms_count[(ml2, ms2)] == 0: del ms_count[(ml2, ms2)]
                assert ms_count.get((ml2, ms2), 0) >= 0
    return out
# lifted verbatim from r2-ch12q.py (chat 76)
def new_terms(l, v): return terms(l, v) - terms(l, v - 2) if v >= 2 else terms(l, v)   # multiset difference (L3081)
# lifted verbatim from r2-ch12q.py (chat 76)
def jc_values(l, k, S2): return sorted({j for (s2, L2), _ in terms(l, k).items() if s2 == S2 for j in range(abs(L2 - s2), L2 + s2 + 1, 2)})
# lifted verbatim from r2-ch12r.py (chat 76)
_T = {}
def TERMS(l, k):
    if (l, k) not in _T: _T[(l, k)] = terms(l, k)
    return _T[(l, k)]
# lifted verbatim from r2-ch12r.py (chat 76)
def L8_at(caps):
    n_max, e_max, l_max, k_max, f_max = caps
    return [(n, l, k, q, e, f, g, S2) for n in range(1, n_max + 1) for l in range(0, min(l_max, n - 1) + 1) for k in range(1, min(k_max, 4 * l + 2) + 1)
            for q in range(0, k + 1) for e in range(1, e_max + 1) for f in range(0, min(f_max, e - 1) + 1) for g in range(0, min(4 * f + 2, q) + 1) for S2 in range(0, k + 1)]
# lifted verbatim from r2-ch12r.py (chat 76)
def phi_at(caps):
    n_max, e_max, l_max, k_max, f_max = caps
    raw = {k: max(L2 + s2 for l in range(l_max + 1) if k <= 4 * l + 2 for (s2, L2) in TERMS(l, k)) for k in range(1, k_max + 1)}
    env = {}; run = 0
    for k in range(1, k_max + 1): run = max(run, raw[k]); env[k] = run
    return raw, env

def B10(g): return sum(g - s + 1 for s in range(g + 1))                      # Λ₁₀ cells over a Λ₈ cell: (2S′, v), 0 ≤ 2S′ ≤ v ≤ g (tower-2.py's fibre)
SH = 'spdf'
def own_max(l, k): return max(L2 + s2 for (s2, L2) in TERMS(l, k))          # the largest 2J_c that occurs among the terms of ℓᵏ
def own_max_S(l, k, S2):                                                     # … among the terms of ℓᵏ carrying the cell's own 2S (L3082's restriction)
    j = jc_values(l, k, S2); return max(j) if j else None

def table(caps):
    raw, env = phi_at(caps); L8c = L8_at(caps)
    n10 = 0; env_cells = 0; env_sum = 0
    A = B = C = D = E = F = 0        # candidate exact counts
    by_shell = defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0])
    for c in L8c:
        l, k, S2, g = c[1], c[2], c[7], c[6]; w = B10(g); n10 += w
        env_cells += w * (env[k] + 1); env_sum += w * env[k]
        om = own_max(l, k); A += w * (om + 1)                                # A: every 2J_c in [0, own max] (all integers)
        oms = own_max_S(l, k, S2); B += w * ((oms + 1) if oms is not None else 0)   # B: [0, own max among terms with the cell's 2S]
        C += w * len(jc_values(l, k, S2))                                   # C: realised values only (§12.11.1 L3082, r2-ch12q)
        D += w * om                                                          # D: the largest 2J_c summed literally
        E += w * ((om - k % 2) // 2 + 1)                                     # E: [k mod 2, own max] in steps of 2
        F += w * (raw[k] + 1)                                                # F: [0, raw φ̂(k)] (the un-enveloped bound over all shells)
        by_shell[(l, k)][0] += w * (om + 1); by_shell[(l, k)][1] += w * (env[k] + 1)
    return dict(raw=raw, env=env, n8=len(L8c), n10=n10, n11=env_cells, envsum=env_sum, A=A, B=B, C=C, D=D, E=E, F=F, shells=by_shell)

ROWS = [((3, 3, 1, 3, 1), 13585, 10585, 77.9), ((4, 4, 1, 6, 1), 226609, 106421, 47.0), ((4, 4, 2, 6, 2), 1225415, 616725, 50.3), ((5, 5, 2, 6, 2), 2341841, 1228816, 52.5)]

# ---- control at the book's caps: the tower's own Λ₁₀ / Λ₁₁ against the fibre sums
L10, L11 = T.L10(), T.L11(); t0 = table((3, 3, 1, 3, 1))
jc11 = defaultdict(set)
for c in L11: jc11[c[2]].add(c[10])
print(f'== control (3,3,1,3,1): tower Λ10 {len(L10):,} = fibre sum {t0["n10"]:,} {len(L10)==t0["n10"]} | tower Λ11 {len(L11):,} = Σ(φ̂(k)+1) over Λ10 {t0["n11"]:,} {len(L11)==t0["n11"]} | 2J_c per k in the tower {dict(sorted((k, (min(v), max(v), len(v))) for k, v in jc11.items()))} = every integer in [0, φ̂(k)] {all(sorted(v)==list(range(max(v)+1)) for v in jc11.values())}')
print(f'   φ̂ raw {t0["raw"]} envelope {t0["env"]} | own max 2J_c by shell: ' + ', '.join(f'{SH[l]}{k} {own_max(l,k)}' for l in range(2) for k in range(1, min(3, 4*l+2)+1)))

# ---- the four rows under the method as written and its readings
print('== L3188–3192 caps | Λ8 | Λ10 | |Λ11| envelope (printed) | exact under A [0,own max] · B [0,own max at own 2S] · C realised (§12.11.1) · D Σ own max · E parity interval · F [0,raw φ̂] (printed) | densities')
dens = {}
for caps, p11, pex, pd in ROWS:
    t = table(caps); dens[caps] = {K: 100 * t[K] / t['n11'] for K in 'ABCDEF'}
    hit = [K for K in 'ABCDEF' if t[K] == pex]
    print(f'   {caps}: Λ8 {t["n8"]:,} | Λ10 {t["n10"]:,} | |Λ11| {t["n11"]:,} (printed {p11:,} {"OK" if t["n11"]==p11 else "MISMATCH"}) | A {t["A"]:,} B {t["B"]:,} C {t["C"]:,} D {t["D"]:,} E {t["E"]:,} F {t["F"]:,} (printed exact {pex:,}: reproduced by {hit if hit else "none"}) | density A {dens[caps]["A"]:.1f} B {dens[caps]["B"]:.1f} C {dens[caps]["C"]:.1f} D/Σφ̂ {100*t["D"]/t["envsum"]:.1f} E {dens[caps]["E"]:.1f} F {dens[caps]["F"]:.1f} | printed {pd}')
    print(f'      shells present {sorted({SH[l] for (l, k) in t["shells"]})} | φ̂ raw {list(t["raw"].values())} envelope {list(t["env"].values())} | per (ℓ,k) exact/envelope under A: ' + ' '.join(f'{SH[l]}{k}:{a:,}/{b:,}' for (l, k), (a, b) in sorted(t["shells"].items())))

# ---- L3194–3195 monotonicity, L3197–3199 the causes
seq = [dens[c]['A'] for c, _, _, _ in ROWS]
print(f'== L3194 "not monotone in the caps" under A: {[round(x, 1) for x in seq]} — falls then rises {seq[0] > seq[1] < seq[2] < seq[3]}; under C (§12.11.1\'s definition): {[round(dens[c]["C"], 1) for c, _, _, _ in ROWS]} monotone falling {all(dens[ROWS[i][0]]["C"] > dens[ROWS[i+1][0]]["C"] for i in range(3))}')
print('== L3194/L3197 "falls … when the d shell opens": ℓ_max by row ' + ', '.join(f'{c} ℓ_max={c[2]}' for c, _, _, _ in ROWS) + ' — the d shell is absent at the 47.0 % row and enters at the 50.3 % row (ℓ ≤ ℓ_max; L3186 names the tuple (n_max, e_max, ℓ_max, k_max, f_max))')
def growth(c1, c2):
    a, b = table(c1), table(c2); return a['A'], b['A'], a['n11'], b['n11']
for c1, c2 in [((3, 3, 1, 3, 1), (4, 4, 1, 6, 1)), ((4, 4, 1, 6, 1), (4, 4, 2, 6, 2)), ((4, 4, 2, 6, 2), (5, 5, 2, 6, 2))]:
    a1, a2, e1, e2 = growth(c1, c2); print(f'   {c1} → {c2}: exact ×{a2/a1:.2f}, envelope ×{e2/e1:.2f} — envelope grows faster {e2/e1 > a2/a1}')
# what each cap change does on its own, from the book's caps: one coordinate at a time, and the d shell alone
print('== single-cap variations from (3,3,1,3,1) under A (which coordinate moves the density):')
for caps in [(4, 3, 1, 3, 1), (3, 4, 1, 3, 1), (3, 3, 2, 3, 1), (3, 3, 1, 6, 1), (3, 3, 1, 3, 2), (4, 4, 1, 3, 1), (4, 4, 1, 6, 1), (4, 4, 2, 6, 1), (4, 4, 2, 3, 1), (3, 3, 2, 6, 1)]:
    t = table(caps); print(f'   {caps}: |Λ11| {t["n11"]:,} exact {t["A"]:,} density {100*t["A"]/t["n11"]:.1f} | φ̂ envelope {list(t["env"].values())}')
# where the shortfall sits at the 47.0 % row: p⁴, p⁵, p⁶ under the running envelope
t = table((4, 4, 1, 6, 1))
print('   (4,4,1,6,1) shortfall by (ℓ,k), envelope − exact under A: ' + ', '.join(f'{SH[l]}{k} {b-a:,} (own max {own_max(l,k)} vs φ̂ {t["env"][k]})' for (l, k), (a, b) in sorted(t['shells'].items()) if b > a) + f' | total {t["n11"]-t["A"]:,}')

# ---- the base "each cell of Λ₁₀" (L3183) read against 12q-01 (v ≡ g mod 2, a term new at v carrying 2S′) and 12r-01 (v ≤ 4f+2−g):
# the same exact/envelope ratio (A) with each Λ₈ cell weighted by its realised (2S′, v) pairs instead of every (2S′, v) of the lattice fibre
def v_real(f, g, s2p, capped): return [v for v in range(s2p, g + 1) if (g - v) % 2 == 0 and (not capped or v <= 4 * f + 2 - g) and any(s2 == s2p for (s2, _) in new_terms(f, v))]
print('== L3183 the base every Λ10 cell: under A the axis-10 conditions do not enter (numerator and |Λ11| run over the same Λ10 cells); with the base restricted to realised (2S′, v) [12q-01 | +12r-01] the ratio would be:')
for caps, _, _, pd in ROWS:
    raw, env = phi_at(caps); out = []
    for capped in (False, True):
        num = den = 0; W = {}
        for c in L8_at(caps):
            l, k, f, g = c[1], c[2], c[5], c[6]
            if (f, g, capped) not in W: W[(f, g, capped)] = sum(len(v_real(f, g, s, capped)) for s in range(g + 1))
            w = W[(f, g, capped)]; num += w * (own_max(l, k) + 1); den += w * (env[k] + 1)
        out.append(f'{100*num/den:.1f} ({num:,} / {den:,})')
    print(f'   {caps}: {out[0]} | {out[1]} — printed {pd}')
# L3179–3181, L3201 against F.3 as printed (L11284–11289): the columns of the standard, counted from the member
mem = r2lib.read_member('The_Method_1_6-2.md').split('\n')

# READ-ch12u — Phase R2, main volume §12.11.1.2 "The conservative share, recomputed under variation" (chat 77)

Member The_Method_1_6-2.md (BUILD90 main, md5 4aef772b…), L3205–L3232 (28 lines, none over 106 characters; §12.11.1.3 opens at L3233), read in full against §12.11.0.1 (L2577–2628; the four-cap table L2593–2597; L2582 and L2607), §12.11.0.8 (L2887–2892, the tick's two sources), the Register (389 at R L1443–1445; 392 at R L1455–1457; 393 at R L1459–1461; 630's neighbour at R L2321), READ-ch12t (12t-01), the banked r2-ch12f (chat 73) and the segment instrument r2-ch12u.py (r2lib by path; build9/src/tgt/analyse of r2-ch12f; every Λ₉ cell at each of the four caps — 1,654 / 19,433 / 44,153 / 83,543 — with the tower's own Λ₉ as the control at the book's caps). Pointers: §12.11.0.1 (L3206) resolves to the heading and to L2607 (`904 of 1,654 cells are conservative — 54.7%`); Registers 389, 392 (L3231) resolve (R L1443, L1455); 392 restates this section's figures and inherits 12u-01, 12u-02 and 12u-03; 393 records the denominator repair L3206–3209 now carries and inherits 12u-01. No lowercase `register NNN` or `A.N` in range. Census rows in range: 688 (not a defect) — CENSUS-CLOSURES-ch12u.tsv.

## A. Deviations (both texts)

**12u-01 · subject matter — the d shell again, at a row where it is absent.** L3226–3227: `Once the d shell is open the share sits at 37–38% and moves by less than a point`; L3222: `It nearly halves when the shells open`. The 37.1 % row (L3218) is (4, 4, 1, 6, 1) with ℓ_max = 1 — s and p shells only under the tuple L3214 names; the d shell enters at the 37.7 % row (MEASURED, r2-ch12u; the same fact as 12t-01 for the density table). The fall from 63.2 % happens at k_max 3 → 6 without any d shell. Register 393 (`both nearly halving when the d shell opens`) and 392 (`once the d shell opens the share sits at 37.1%, 37.7% and 37.9%`) repeat it.

**12u-02 · subject matter — "less than a point across a fiftyfold growth" joins two ranges.** L3227: `moves by less than a point across a fiftyfold growth in cells`; Register 392: `moving less than a point across a fiftyfold growth in cells`. MEASURED (r2-ch12u): the fiftyfold growth is Λ₉ from the book's caps to (5,5,2,6,2) — 1,654 → 83,543 = 50.5× (composable 60.8×) — and across that range the share moves 25.3 points (63.2 → 37.9). The range over which it moves less than a point (0.8; all-cells 0.9) is rows 2–4, 19,433 → 83,543 = 4.3× (composable 4.4×). The sentence is true of neither range as written.

**12u-03 · subject matter — the conservative share is named "reversibility".** L3228–3229: `**reversibility settles near three cells in eight among the composable, and the book's own caps overstate it by two thirds.**`; Register 392: `reversibility settles near three cells in eight`. The quantity of the table (L3212–3213, `count those with g = q`) is the conservative share. Reversibility in §12.11.0.1's own usage is a morphism having a reverse (L2607: `389 morphisms have a reverse`; r2-ch12f/r2lib: cells whose (src, tgt) pair has a reverse edge), and §12.11.0.8 (L2887–2888) splits the tick k − g = (k − q) + (q − g): a conservative cell zeroes the second term only and may still tick. MEASURED (r2-ch12u, analyse at the four caps): cells whose object pair has a reverse are 389 of 1,169 = 33.3 %, 1,771 of 16,150 = 11.0 %, 4,203 of 37,430 = 11.2 %, 8,046 of 71,087 = 11.3 % — one cell in nine above the book's caps, not three in eight, and the book's caps overstate it threefold, not by two thirds. The conservative share itself (63.2 / 37.1 / 37.7 / 37.9) is right; the name attached to it at L3228 is not the book's.

## B. Verified (all MEASURED; r2-ch12u.py)

- L3216–3220 every entry of the table reproduces: |Λ₉| 1,654 / 19,433 / 44,153 / 83,543; composable (target a legal source) 1,169 / 16,150 / 37,430 / 71,087; conservative among the composable 739 / 5,986 / 14,114 / 26,921; share 63.2 / 37.1 / 37.7 / 37.9. The tower's own Λ₉ equals build9 at the book's caps (1,654, same cell set).
- L3206–3208 both denominators: 904 of 1,654 = 54.7 % over every cell; 739 of 1,169 = 63.2 % over the composable — as r2-ch12f banked (chat 73) and here.
- L3223–3224 the all-cells share 54.7 → 34.4 / 35.1 / 35.3 (§12.11.0.1's L2594–2597 reproduce: objects 33 / 101 / 155 / 214, edges 739 / 5,986 / 14,114 / 26,921, conservative 904 / 6,693 / 15,509 / 29,489).
- The conservative-among-composable count equals §12.11.0.1's edge count at all four caps (739 / 5,986 / 14,114 / 26,921), and the all-cells conservative count equals the edge count including non-object targets (904 of 1,254 at the book's caps): a joined object pair (n, ℓ, k, 2S) → (e, f, g, 2S′) is joined by one cell per q ∈ [g, k], of which exactly one has q = g. The share is therefore 1 / (mean cells per edge) — a structural identity, not a coincidence of the two tables.
- L3229 `overstate it by two thirds`: 63.2 / 37.9 = 1.67. L3228 `three cells in eight` = 37.5 against 37.1–37.9. L3230 `the instability is in the caps and not in the choice of population`: both shares fall at the same step (×0.59 composable, ×0.63 all cells) and both then move under a point.

## C. Incidental

- L3222 `nearly halves`: the composable share falls to 0.59 of itself, the all-cells share to 0.63 — a loose "nearly"; not a deviation.
- L3216–3220 the table is a column-dump (four-gap columns) and L3222–3224 a 4-space paragraph rendering as code — production class.
- L3210 `with the method named, its input set named, and every input printed` — the three-part statement of 12t-03 (no refutation test named); further site.
- Register 393's account (`Repaired by naming both denominators where the second is stated`) matches L3206–3209 as printed; Register L2321's `1,169 of 1,654 = 70.7%` (the reachable fraction) is the composable share of the same population — for the Register's segment.

# READ-ch12y.md — Phase R2 read of main §12.11.2 "Three excluded forms, and the fold has a name" (L3363–3393), chat 78

Instrument: r2-ch12y.py (golden r2-ch12y.out). Support and definitions recovered are stated per item. No repairs (chat 67 hold).

## A — deviations (both texts)

**12y-01 — "two constraint forms" against §17.2's printed three, and the form mislabelled.**
Main L3364: "Chapter 17 excluded two constraint forms — sums and differences." and L3374: "precisely Chapter 17's two exclusions wearing physics". The cited chapter's own exclusion line, §17.2 L4802: "Projections, maxima, minima and constants qualify; **sums, products and differences do not**" — three excluded forms, and they are **axis** exclusions (E2, which axes may be adjoined), not constraint exclusions. The constraint door (§17.3, E3) **admits** constraints on a difference under convexity (L4817 "for a constraint on a DIFFERENCE the criterion is convexity, which is proved here", L4827 criterion), so "constraint forms ... excluded" is doubly against the source. MC L1254 carries the same reading twice ("Two constraint forms were already excluded — sums and differences (§17.2)"; "precisely §17.2's two exclusions") and inherits. §36.3 L9910 restates the three-excluded-forms frame on the potential (sum, difference, symmetric) — consistent with the sum+difference+symmetric triple, unaffected by the count-of-Ch.17-exclusions error. For R3; no withdrawal.

**12y-02 — the (2S,2L,2J) presentation's 2,443 meets: population unstated, count not recovered.**
Main L3377: "as (2S,2L,2J) (2,443 meets)". The population is printed nowhere. Measured over eleven candidate level populations (levels = (2S,2L,2J) fine-structure triples of terms by microstate enumeration), none yields 2,443 in any column (unordered/ordered, meet/join):
realised shells at caps (s¹ s² p¹ p² p³) n 11: meets 23; p every k n 10: 22; p+d n 55: 589; s+p+d n 55: 589; s+p+d+f n 190: 7,314; d alone n 54: 558; f alone n 189: 7,173; f k ≤ 7: 7,173; ℓ ≤ 3, k ≤ 3 n 50: 374; ℓ ≤ 2, k ≤ 3 n 28: 126; p+d+f n 190: 7,314 (unordered; ordered are double). The qualitative half of the sentence — "the triangle's first meet failure manufactures J = ½ from S = L = 0" — **does** reproduce: the first failing meet in lexicographic pair order is (2S,2L,2J) = (0,4,4) ∧ (1,0,1) = (0,0,1) on the realised-caps population (and the same manufactured cell (0,0,1) on p+d, s+p+d, s+p+d+f), and the triangle grid's own first failing meet at cap 6 is (0,1,1) ∧ (1,0,1) = (0,0,1). # r2-ch12y.py — Phase R2, main §12.11.2 "Three excluded forms, and the fold has a name" (L3363–3393), chat 78.
# Re-measured on all cells or pairs: the conjugation symmetry terms(ℓᵏ) = terms(ℓ^(4ℓ+2−k)) for every k on the p and
# d shells (L3365–3366); max2J(ℓ,k) unimodal, peaking at half filling, 25 at f⁷, zero at closure (L3368–3369) and its
# conjugation symmetry; min(g, 4f+2−g) invariant under the fold (L3368); the axis-9 envelope gap parity 5 / fold 1 /
# both 1 and the axis-11 gap ceiling 16 / parity 24 / triangle 17 at the caps of §7.4 (L3371–3372); the five
# presentations of the exact coupling region and their closure failures 50,592 / 52,080 / 17,856 / 7,254 / 2,443 with
# the first meet failure manufacturing J = ½ from S = L = 0 (L3375–3378); the four-cap join/meet check of
# {|2L−2S| ≤ 2J ≤ 2L+2S} — 0 join failures and 2,862 / 12,489 / 40,887 / 110,229 failing meets at caps 6, 8, 10, 12,
# unordered pairs per MC L1256 — and the parity-congruence collapse, 1,848 join failures at cap 6 (L3385–3390).
# Cross-sites: main L8290 (U4), MC L1254/L1260. tower-2.py by path via r2lib. Deterministic (no wall-clock).
import importlib.util, os, itertools
from collections import Counter
H = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
s = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('r2lib', os.path.join(H, 'r2lib.py')); r2lib = importlib.util.module_from_spec(s); s.loader.exec_module(r2lib); T = r2lib.load_tower()
PHI = T.PHI

# lifted verbatim from r2-ch12q.py (chat 76) — LS terms of ℓ^k by microstate enumeration (L3059–3063)
def terms(l, k):
    if k == 0: return Counter({(0, 0): 1})
    orbs = [(ml, ms) for ml in range(-l, l + 1) for ms in (-1, 1)]
    ms_count = Counter((2 * sum(o[0] for o in c), sum(o[1] for o in c)) for c in itertools.combinations(orbs, k))
    out = Counter()
    while ms_count:
        ML2 = max(m for m, _ in ms_count); MS2 = max(sv for m, sv in ms_count if m == ML2)
        out[(MS2, ML2)] += 1
        for ml2 in range(-ML2, ML2 + 1, 2):
            for ms2 in range(-MS2, MS2 + 1, 2):
                ms_count[(ml2, ms2)] -= 1
                if ms_count[(ml2, ms2)] == 0: del ms_count[(ml2, ms2)]
                assert ms_count.get((ml2, ms2), 0) >= 0
    return out

# lifted verbatim from r2-ch12q.py (chat 76)
def jc_values(l, k, S2): return sorted({j for (s2, L2), _ in terms(l, k).items() if s2 == S2 for j in range(abs(L2 - s2), L2 + s2 + 1, 2)})

def max2J(l, k): return max(s2 + L2 for (s2, L2) in terms(l, k))

# ---- L3365–3366: terms(ℓᵏ) = terms(ℓ^(4ℓ+2−k)) for every k on the p and d shells
print('== L3365–3366 conjugation symmetry of terms, as multisets:')
for l, nm in [(1, 'p'), (2, 'd')]:
    ok = all(terms(l, k) == terms(l, 4 * l + 2 - k) for k in range(0, 4 * l + 2 + 1))
    print(f'   {nm} shell, every k in 0..{4*l+2}: terms(ℓᵏ) == terms(ℓ^(4ℓ+2−k)) {ok}')

# ---- L3368–3369: max2J(ℓ,k) — unimodal, peak at half filling, 25 at f⁷, zero at closure; symmetric under the fold
print('== L3368–3369 max2J(ℓ,k):')
for l, nm in [(1, 'p'), (2, 'd'), (3, 'f')]:
    vals = [max2J(l, k) for k in range(0, 4 * l + 2 + 1)]
    pk = vals.index(max(vals))
    rising = all(vals[i] <= vals[i + 1] for i in range(pk)); falling = all(vals[i] >= vals[i + 1] for i in range(pk, len(vals) - 1))
    sym = all(vals[k] == vals[4 * l + 2 - k] for k in range(len(vals)))
    print(f'   {nm}: {vals} | unimodal {rising and falling} | peak at k = {pk} (half filling {2*l+1}: {pk == 2*l+1}) | zero at k=0 and closure {vals[0] == 0 and vals[-1] == 0} | symmetric under k↦4ℓ+2−k {sym}')
print(f'   25 at f⁷: max2J(3,7) = {max2J(3,7)}')

# ---- L3368: min(g, 4f+2−g) invariant under g ↦ 4f+2−g (the fold), f = 0, 1
inv = all(min(g, 4 * f + 2 - g) == min(4 * f + 2 - g, g) and min(g, 4 * f + 2 - g) == min(4 * f + 2 - (4 * f + 2 - g), 4 * f + 2 - g) for f in (0, 1) for g in range(0, 4 * f + 3))
print(f'== L3368 min(g, 4f+2−g) invariant under the fold g ↦ 4f+2−g, f = 0..1, all g: {inv}')

# ---- stages
L8, L9, L10 = T.L8(), T.L9(), T.L10()
spin = {}
for (f, g) in sorted({(c[5], c[6]) for c in L8}):
    spin[(f, g)] = sorted({s2 for (s2, _) in terms(f, g)})

# ---- L3371–3372 axis 9's gap at the caps of §7.4: parity / fold / both over the (f, g) support
print('== L3371–3372 axis 9 gap — support = realised (f, g) of Λ8; envelope 2S′ ∈ [0, g]; exact = spin set of f^g by microstate enumeration:')
par = fld = both = adm = rea = 0
for (f, g) in sorted(spin):
    ex = set(spin[(f, g)]); cap = min(g, 4 * f + 2 - g)
    chk = ex == {sv for sv in range(0, g + 1) if (g - sv) % 2 == 0 and sv <= cap}
    adm += g + 1; rea += len(ex); det = []
    for sv in range(0, g + 1):
        if sv in ex: continue
        p = (g - sv) % 2 == 1; fl = sv > cap
        if p and fl: both += 1; det.append(f'{sv}:both')
        elif p: par += 1; det.append(f'{sv}:parity')
        elif fl: fld += 1; det.append(f'{sv}:fold')
    print(f'   (f,g)=({f},{g}): exact {sorted(ex)} == parity∧fold set {chk} | excluded {" ".join(det) if det else "—"}')
print(f'   TOTAL admitted {adm}, realised {rea}, gap {adm - rea}: parity {par}, fold {fld}, both {both}   (printed: parity 5, fold 1, both 1)')

# ---- L3372 axis 11's gap: support = realised (ℓ, k, 2S) of Λ10; envelope 2J_c ∈ [0, φ̂(k)]; exact = jc_values(ℓ, k, 2S);
# attribution in order: ceiling (2J_c > max2J(ℓ,k)) → parity (2J_c ≢ k mod 2) → triangle (the rest)
sup = sorted({(c[1], c[2], c[7]) for c in L10})
full = sorted({(l, k, s2) for (l, k) in {(c[1], c[2]) for c in L10} for s2 in range(0, k + 1)})
print(f'== L3372 axis 11 gap — support = realised (ℓ,k,2S) of Λ10 ({len(sup)} triples) == all 2S ∈ [0,k] over realised (ℓ,k): {sup == full} | φ̂ = {PHI}')
ce = pa = tr = adm = rea = 0; ce_i = pa_i = tr_i = 0
for (l, k, s2) in sup:
    ex = set(jc_values(l, k, s2)); m = max2J(l, k)
    adm += PHI[k] + 1; rea += len(ex); det = []
    for j in range(0, PHI[k] + 1):
        if j in ex: continue
        # independent (overlapping) counts, for the record
        if j > m: ce_i += 1
        if (j - k) % 2: pa_i += 1
        if j <= m and (j - k) % 2 == 0: tr_i += 1
        # attribution, ceiling first
        if j > m: ce += 1; det.append(f'{j}:ceiling')
        elif (j - k) % 2: pa += 1; det.append(f'{j}:parity')
        else: tr += 1; det.append(f'{j}:triangle')
    print(f'   (ℓ,k,2S)=({l},{k},{s2}): exact {sorted(ex) if ex else "∅"} | max2J {m} | excluded {" ".join(det) if det else "—"}')
print(f'   TOTAL admitted {adm}, realised {rea}, gap {adm - rea}: ceiling {ce}, parity {pa}, triangle {tr}   (printed: ceiling 16, parity 24, triangle 17)')
print(f'   independent (overlapping) counts for the record: >max2J {ce_i}, wrong parity {pa_i}, within-ceiling right-parity unrealised {tr_i}')

# ---- L3375–3378 the five presentations of the exact coupling region
def first_fail(X):
    """first unordered pair (lexicographic scan) whose componentwise meet leaves X; returns (a, b, meet) or None"""
    S = set(X); L = sorted(X)
    for i in range(len(L)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(L)):
            mt = tuple(min(a, b) for a, b in zip(L[i], L[j]))
            if mt not in S: return L[i], L[j], mt
    return None

E9  = [c for c in L9 if c[8] in spin[(c[5], c[6])]]
PAR = [c for c in L9 if (c[6] - c[8]) % 2 == 0]
CAP = [c for c in L9 if c[8] <= 4 * c[5] + 2 - c[6]]
PC  = [c[:8] + ((c[6] - c[8]) // 2,) for c in E9]
print('== L3375–3378 five presentations — r2lib.closure over ordered pairs incl. self (n², join fails, meet fails); halves are the unordered counts:')
for X, lab, printed in [(E9, 'as 2S′ (exact: parity ∧ fold)', '50,592'), (PAR, 'as parity alone', '52,080'), (CAP, 'as the min-cap alone', '17,856'), (PC, 'as pair count p = (g−2S′)/2 on the exact set', '7,254')]:
    n2, jl, ml = r2lib.closure(X)
    print(f'   [{lab}] n {len(X):,} | join fails {jl:,} (unord {jl//2:,}) | meet fails {ml:,} (unord {ml//2:,}) | j+m {jl+ml:,} (unord {(jl+ml)//2:,})   printed {printed}')

def levels(shells):
    out = set()
    for (l, k) in shells:
        for (s2, L2) in terms(l, k):
            for j in range(abs(L2 - s2), L2 + s2 + 1, 2): out.add((s2, L2, j))
    return sorted(out)
print('== L3377 (2S,2L,2J) presentation — candidate level populations:')
cands = [('levels of the realised shells at caps (s¹ s² p¹ p² p³)', [(0,1),(0,2),(1,1),(1,2),(1,3)]),
         ('levels of the p shell, every k', [(1,k) for k in range(0,7)]),
         ('levels of p and d, every k', [(1,k) for k in range(0,7)] + [(2,k) for k in range(0,11)]),
         ('levels of s, p and d, every k', [(0,k) for k in range(0,3)] + [(1,k) for k in range(0,7)] + [(2,k) for k in range(0,11)]),
         ('levels of s, p, d and f, every k', [(0,k) for k in range(0,3)] + [(1,k) for k in range(0,7)] + [(2,k) for k in range(0,11)] + [(3,k) for k in range(0,15)])]
for lab, sh in cands:
    X = levels(sh); n2, jl, ml = r2lib.closure(X); ff = first_fail(X)
    print(f'   [{lab}] n {len(X)} | join fails {jl:,} (unord {jl//2:,}) | meet fails {ml:,} (unord {ml//2:,}) | first failing meet {ff[0]} ∧ {ff[1]} = {ff[2]}' if ff else f'   [{lab}] n {len(X)} | no meet failure')

# ---- L3376 "failures": distinct unordered pairs failing either operation (overlap of the join- and meet-failing pair sets)
def failing_pairs(X):
    S = set(X); L = sorted(X); jset = mset = both = 0
    for i in range(len(L)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(L)):
            jn = tuple(max(a, b) for a, b in zip(L[i], L[j])) not in S
            mt = tuple(min(a, b) for a, b in zip(L[i], L[j])) not in S
            if jn and mt: both += 1
            elif jn: jset += 1
            elif mt: mset += 1
    return jset, mset, both, jset + mset + both
print('== L3376 distinct failing unordered pairs (join-only, meet-only, both, total):')
for X, lab, printed in [(E9, 'as 2S′', '50,592'), (PAR, 'as parity alone', '52,080')]:
    jo, mo, bo, tot = failing_pairs(X)
    print(f'   [{lab}] join-only {jo:,} | meet-only {mo:,} | both {bo:,} | pairs failing either {tot:,}   printed {printed}')

# ---- L3377 wider population sweep for the 2,443
print('== L3377 (2S,2L,2J) sweep — further candidate populations:')
sweeps = [('d shell alone, every k', [(2,k) for k in range(0,11)]),
          ('f shell alone, every k', [(3,k) for k in range(0,15)]),
          ('f shell, k ≤ 7', [(3,k) for k in range(0,8)]),
          ('ℓ ≤ 3, k ≤ 3 (the k cap of §7.4)', [(l,k) for l in range(0,4) for k in range(0, min(3,4*l+2)+1)]),
          ('ℓ ≤ 2, k ≤ 3', [(l,k) for l in range(0,3) for k in range(0, min(3,4*l+2)+1)]),
          ('p, d and f, every k', [(1,k) for k in range(0,7)] + [(2,k) for k in range(0,11)] + [(3,k) for k in range(0,15)])]
for lab, sh in sweeps:
    X = levels(sh); n2, jl, ml = r2lib.closure(X)
    print(f'   [{lab}] n {len(X)} | join fails {jl:,} (unord {jl//2:,}) | meet fails {ml:,} (unord {ml//2:,})')

# ---- L3385–3390 the four-cap check of the triangle, unordered pairs (MC L1256)
print('== L3385–3390 T = {(2L,2S,2J): |2L−2S| ≤ 2J ≤ 2L+2S} on the box {0..cap}³:')
for cap, printed in [(6, '2,862'), (8, '12,489'), (10, '40,887'), (12, '110,229')]:
    Tset = [(a, b, j) for a in range(cap + 1) for b in range(cap + 1) for j in range(abs(a - b), min(a + b, cap) + 1)]
    n2, jl, ml = r2lib.closure(Tset)
    print(f'   cap {cap}: |T| {len(Tset):,} | join fails {jl} | meet fails unordered {ml//2:,}   printed {printed}')
    if cap == 6:
        ff = first_fail(Tset)
        print(f'      first failing meet: {ff[0]} ∧ {ff[1]} = {ff[2]}')
        Tp = [t for t in Tset if (t[0] + t[1] - t[2]) % 2 == 0]
        n2p, jlp, mlp = r2lib.closure(Tp)
        print(f'      + parity congruence 2J ≡ 2L+2S (mod 2): |T∩par| {len(Tp):,} | join fails unordered {jlp//2:,} (ordered {jlp:,})   printed 1,848 | meet fails unordered {mlp//2:,}')

## A — deviations (both texts)

**12z-01 — "The origins table of Chapter 7 has four rows" against the printed seven-row table.**
Main L3398: "The origins table of Chapter 7 has four rows." The printed table (§7.1 L1753–1760) has **seven** constraint rows carrying **four** distinct origin values, and §7.1's own summary line L1762 says so: "Seven constraints, four origins, and nothing else." MC L1264 carries the same reading ("The origins table (§7.1) has four rows — Pauli, the hydrogenic solution and counting give single-coordinate exact bounds ...") and inherits. Counted clerically in r2-ch12z.py: rows 7, distinct origins 4 (Pauli, counting, hydrogenic, vector coupling). The intended object is plainly the four origins; the printed word is "rows". For R3; no withdrawal.

**12z-02 — one word pair, two measured distinctions: the dichotomy's "exact / envelope" against the grading column's.**
The dichotomy (L3395–3396): "Counting coordinates close exactly. Coupling coordinates close as envelopes. There is no third kind in this object." Measured, both halves are true in the **bound-versus-physics** sense: every counting bound's interval is fully realised at every parent value of Λ₈ (five bounds, all True), while the first coupling constraint 2S ≤ k admits 14 values and the spin sets of ℓᵏ realise 7 (gap 7), as axis 9 admits 16 and realises 9 (r2-ch12y). But the tower table's grading column (L2937–2939) grades **Λ₉ "exact · composes" and Λ₁₀ "exact"** — coupling axes graded exact — and in the **closure** sense every stage is exact: E(Λ₈) = E(Λ₉) = 0 re-measured here by the ambient-box sweep (6,912 and 27,648 cells; all six stages per Register 249, r2-ch12r). So "exact/envelope" names the bound-versus-physics distinction at L3395 and L3136–3137 ("counting axes stay exact and all three coupling axes stay envelopes"), and a different distinction — the one §12.11.3.1's provenance reading refines — in the grading column, with the printed text silent on the shift. The 12o-01 class (one word, two quantities). MC "Law versus extent" (L1264) is the explicit harmonisation and the candidate R3 resolution; kin to SWEEP-C's §17.2 classification finding (one class true, one false, text silent on which). **This closes DEFERRED's 12e-05** (axis 9 exact or envelope): axis 9 is exact in the closure sense (E(Λ₉) = 0, measured) and as graded, and an envelope in the dichotomy's bound sense (gap 7, measured) — both, sense-dependent. L3136–3137's restatement is absorbed here as a site; 12j-01 (the provenance column's "three values, not two" against the grading column's two) settles at the §12.11.3.1 segment as planned. For R3; no withdrawal.

# r2-ch12z.py — Phase R2, main §12.11.3 "The dichotomy" (L3394–3408), chat 78.
# Measured: the dichotomy's two halves — every counting coordinate's realised values fill its bound interval at every
# parent value of Λ₈ (close exactly), while the first coupling constraint 2S ≤ k admits more than the physics realises
# (closes as an envelope; the spin set of ℓᵏ by microstate enumeration) — L3395–3396 and the §7.1 origins-table claim
# (L3398–3399); E(Λ₈) = E(Λ₉) = 0 by the ambient-box sweep (the closure sense of "exact", the 12e-05 disposition's
# first pillar; the bound sense is r2-ch12y's axis-9 gap 16 admitted / 9 realised); the §7.1 table's row and origin
# counts against L3398's "four rows"; the Spectra Compendium Part II channel table counted from its own rows against
# the printed 596 / 477 / 119 / 28 / 70 / 3,342 / 2,269 / 1,577 of 1,738 on 392 / 78 no-triple / 126 untested —
# the current record behind L3406's record-carried "153 channels" (registers 630–631; B.2's disclosed drift).
# tower-2.py by path via r2lib. Deterministic (no wall-clock).
import importlib.util, os, itertools, re
from collections import Counter
import numpy as np
H = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
s = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('r2lib', os.path.join(H, 'r2lib.py')); r2lib = importlib.util.module_from_spec(s); s.loader.exec_module(r2lib); T = r2lib.load_tower()

# lifted verbatim from r2-ch12q.py (chat 76) — LS terms of ℓ^k by microstate enumeration (L3059–3063)
def terms(l, k):
    if k == 0: return Counter({(0, 0): 1})
    orbs = [(ml, ms) for ml in range(-l, l + 1) for ms in (-1, 1)]
    ms_count = Counter((2 * sum(o[0] for o in c), sum(o[1] for o in c)) for c in itertools.combinations(orbs, k))
    out = Counter()
    while ms_count:
        ML2 = max(m for m, _ in ms_count); MS2 = max(sv for m, sv in ms_count if m == ML2)
        out[(MS2, ML2)] += 1
        for ml2 in range(-ML2, ML2 + 1, 2):
            for ms2 in range(-MS2, MS2 + 1, 2):
                ms_count[(ml2, ms2)] -= 1
                if ms_count[(ml2, ms2)] == 0: del ms_count[(ml2, ms2)]
                assert ms_count.get((ml2, ms2), 0) >= 0
    return out

# lifted verbatim from r2-ch12r.py (chat 76) — |ℛ(X)| by sweeping every cell of the ambient box
def Rbox(X, extra_slices=None):
    """|ℛ(X)| by sweeping every cell of the ambient box ∏ Âᵢ(X): x ∈ ℛ(X) iff xᵢ ≤ φ̂ᵢⱼ(xⱼ) for all i ≠ j (§6.1 L1540)."""
    A = np.array(X, dtype=np.int64); d = A.shape[1]; vals = [np.unique(A[:, i]) for i in range(d)]
    phi = {}
    for i in range(d):
        for j in range(d):
            if i == j: continue
            m = np.full(int(A[:, j].max()) + 1, -1, dtype=np.int64)
            for v in vals[j]: m[v] = A[A[:, j] <= v, i].max()
            phi[(i, j)] = m
    box = int(np.prod([len(v) for v in vals]))
    if extra_slices is None:
        G = np.array(np.meshgrid(*vals, indexing='ij')).reshape(d, -1).T
        ok = np.ones(len(G), dtype=bool)
        for (i, j), m in phi.items(): ok &= G[:, i] <= m[G[:, j]]
        return box, int(ok.sum()), set(map(tuple, G[ok])) == set(map(tuple, A))

L8, L9 = T.L8(), T.L9()

# ---- L3395 "Counting coordinates close exactly": each counting bound's interval is filled at every parent value of Λ8
print('== L3395 counting coordinates — realised values against the bound interval, over every parent value of Λ8:')
def fills(pairs, lab):
    ok = all(sorted(v) == list(range(min(v), max(v) + 1)) and (min(v), max(v)) == b for v, b in pairs)
    print(f'   {lab}: full interval at every parent value {ok}')
by = lambda key, val: [(sorted({val(c) for c in L8 if key(c) == kv}), kv) for kv in sorted({key(c) for c in L8})]
NMAX, EMAX, LMAX, KMAX, FMAX = 3, 3, 1, 3, 1
fills([(v, (0, min(LMAX, kv - 1))) for v, kv in by(lambda c: c[0], lambda c: c[1])], 'ℓ ≤ n−1        (per n)')
fills([(v, (1, min(KMAX, 4 * kv + 2))) for v, kv in by(lambda c: c[1], lambda c: c[2])], 'k ≤ 2(2ℓ+1)    (per ℓ)')
fills([(v, (0, kv)) for v, kv in by(lambda c: c[2], lambda c: c[3])], 'q ≤ k          (per k)')
fills([(v, (0, min(FMAX, kv - 1))) for v, kv in by(lambda c: c[4], lambda c: c[5])], 'f ≤ e−1        (per e)')
fills([(v, (0, min(4 * kv[0] + 2, kv[1]))) for v, kv in by(lambda c: (c[5], c[3]), lambda c: c[6])], 'g ≤ 2(2f+1), g ≤ q (per (f,q))')

# ---- L3395–3396 "Coupling coordinates close as envelopes. ... the first coupling constraint was already in §7.1":
# 2S ≤ k admits, the spin set of ℓᵏ realises
print('== L3395–3396 the first coupling constraint 2S ≤ k (§7.1 row 7) — admitted vs the spin set of ℓᵏ:')
adm = rea = 0
for (l, k) in sorted({(c[1], c[2]) for c in L8}):
    sp = sorted({s2 for (s2, _) in terms(l, k)})
    adm += k + 1; rea += len(sp)
    print(f'   (ℓ,k)=({l},{k}): admitted [0..{k}] ({k+1}), physics realises {sp} ({len(sp)})')
print(f'   TOTAL admitted {adm}, realised {rea} — an envelope with gap {adm - rea}: the coupling half of the dichotomy, measured')

# ---- 12e-05 disposition, closure sense: E = 0 by the ambient-box sweep at Λ8 and Λ9
for X, lab, exp in [(L8, 'Λ8', 976), (L9, 'Λ9', 1654)]:
    box, r, eq = Rbox(X)
    print(f'== E({lab}) by the box sweep: ambient {box:,} | |ℛ| {r:,} | ℛ(X) = X {eq} | E = {r - len(X)}   (|{lab}| {len(X):,}, expected {exp:,})')

# ---- L3398 "The origins table of Chapter 7 has four rows" — the printed table counted
M = r2lib.read_member('The_Method_1_6-2.md').split('\n')
rows = [M[i] for i in range(1753, 1760)]
origins = []
for r in rows:
    o = r.split(None, 1)[1] if '≤' in r.split()[0] else re.split(r'\s{2,}', r.strip(), 1)[1]
    origins.append(o.strip())
canon = sorted({('hydrogenic' if 'hydrogenic' in o else 'Pauli' if 'Pauli' in o else 'counting' if 'counting' in o else 'vector coupling') for o in origins})
print(f'== L3398 §7.1 table (L1754–1760): constraint rows {len(rows)} | distinct origins {len(canon)} {canon} | L1762 states "Seven constraints, four origins"')

# ---- L3406 "all 153 channels" — record-carried (registers 630–631); the current record counted from the SC's own table
S = r2lib.read_member('The_Method_1_6___Spectra_Compendium-2.md').split('\n')
stop = next(i for i, l in enumerate(S) if '596 channel rows across' in l)
crows = []
for l in S[:stop]:
    if l.startswith('|'):
        f = [x.strip() for x in l.strip().strip('|').split('|')]
        if len(f) == 11 and f[0] not in ('species',) and not set(f[0]) <= {'-', ' '}: crows.append(f)
lv = [int(r[3]) for r in crows]; ic = [int(r[4]) for r in crows]
br = [r[5] for r in crows]
bt = [tuple(int(x.replace(',', '')) for x in b.split('/')) for b in br if '/' in b]
nt = sum(1 for b in br if 'no-triple' in b); ut = sum(1 for b in br if 'untested' in b)
species = sorted({r[0] for r in crows}); elements = sorted({r[0].split()[0] for r in crows})
print(f'== L3406/L10169/SC L994 — SC Part II channel table, counted from its own rows:')
print(f'   rows {len(crows)} (printed 596) | series ≥ 3 members {sum(1 for x in lv if x >= 3)} (477) | two-member {sum(1 for x in lv if x == 2)} (119)')
sp2 = sorted({' '.join(r[0].split()[:2]) for r in crows})
multi = sorted({' '.join(x.split()[:2]) for x in species if len(x.split()) > 2})
print(f'   elements {len(elements)} (28) | species: distinct row labels {len(species)}, element+stage pairs {len(sp2)} (printed 70) | labels beyond element+stage collapse onto {len(multi)} species: {multi}')
print(f'   levels {sum(lv):,} (3,342) | interior cells {sum(ic):,} (2,269)')
print(f'   bracket rows {len(bt)} (392): {sum(a for a, b in bt):,} of {sum(b for a, b in bt):,} (1,577 of 1,738) | no-triple {nt} (78) | untested {ut} (126)')
print(f'   L3406\'s "all 153 channels" has no current table: the first collection\'s count, record-carried per B.2\'s disclosure (main L10203–10208; registers 630–631, 1578, 1699–1700)')

# READ-ch13a.md — Phase R2 read of main §12.11.3.1 "Where each bound comes from, and why 9, 10 and 11 differ" (L3409–3456), chat 78

Instrument: r2-ch13a.py (golden r2-ch13a.out). No repairs (chat 67 hold).

## A — deviations (both texts)

**13a-01 — the withdrawn 2,475 standing at two further sites, one with a failed citation.**
L3477 (§12.11.5): "recomputed; **the 2,475 previously printed here is withdrawn**." Yet L3434 (this range) prints "§A.15 and register 230 record what it costs, 2,475 cells of the cylinder", and L914 prints "The tight K has two parents and costs the cylinder 2,475 cells." The L3434 citation fails both ways: **A.15's printed text (L10054–10071) contains no 2,475** — it is the two-bands result (B_k a sublattice, C not) — and **register 230's printed body is the kind-coordinate entry** ("APPENDIX D'S KIND COORDINATE DISAGREES WITH PART III'S TITLE"), also without it. Measured: the tight-K cuts are 15,150 (Λ₁₂ 70,905 → 55,755) and 45,450 (Λ₁₃ 199,130 → 153,680) — the figures L3477 prints as the recompute — and no natural cut equals 2,475. Joins 12q-06's sites (L3067's "3.5 %", the L2533 Figure 12.4 caption); the residue set for R3 is L914, L2533, L3067, L3434, with L3477's withdrawal governing (the later line). For R3; no withdrawal of the recorded texts.

**13a-02 — "the largest 2J" for "the largest 2J_c": the main's sentence false as printed, the MC's correct.**
L3439–3440: "φ̂ = {1: 3, 2: 4, 3: 5}, and **the largest 2J actually realised at each occupancy** is {1: 3, 2: 4, 3: 5}." Measured: the largest **2J** per k over Λ₁₃ is **{1: 6, 2: 7, 3: 8}** — not φ̂ — while the largest **2J_c** per k over Λ₁₁ is {1: 3, 2: 4, 3: 5}, exactly φ̂. MC L1264 prints "the largest 2J_c the set actually realises" — correct. A coordinate-name slip that falsifies the printed sentence while the intended identity (φ̂ = the envelope of the realised 2J_c extent) is exact. For R3; no withdrawal.

## B — verified (measured, r2-ch13a.py)

- L3413–3428 the thirteen bounds "verified against the construction, cell by cell": all thirteen hold at every cell of Λ₁₃ (199,130 cells; zero violations per bound).
- L3428–3429 "The provenance column has three values, not two": tabulated — law × 11 (D1–10, D13), extent × 1 (D11), law-weakened × 1 (D12).
- L3435–3436: **39,375** of Λ₁₂'s 70,905 cells sit at f below the cap — exact.

# READ-ch13b.md — Phase R2, chat 79, segment 1 — main §12.11.4 (L3457–3461) and §12.11.5 (L3462–3481)

Instrument: `r2-ch13b.py` (banked, r2-ch13b.out 3,712 B · md5 4613302c… · ≈ 2 s). Clerical: `r2-tools.py lines|pointers|figures|census|layout 3457 3481`; manual grep for lowercase `register NNN` and `A.N` returned none in range. Every figure in range was greped across all six volumes; every pointer resolved to heading **and** claim. Findings are recorded, never repaired (chat 67 hold).

## A — deviations

**13b-01 · L3475–3477 — "the tight two-parent K" names two different rules across the volumes, and the printed cut is the one-sided one.** PRINTED L3475–3478: `The boundary: the tight two-parent K — bounded by J_c on the A side and f on the B side — is the first bridge between the cylinder's two ends other than q, and it breaks the factorisation by **15,150 cells at Λ₁₂ and 45,450 at Λ₁₃**, 21.4% and 22.8% of the product`. SOURCE: MC L1696, the entry *The recoupling bound*, prints `loose: 2K ≤ 2J_c + 2f_max (one parent). exact: |2J_c−2f| ≤ 2K ≤ 2J_c+2f step 2 (two parents)`, cited to Wigner 1931 and Racah 1942 — the physical vector-coupling rule, two-sided and parity-stepped. MC L1264 restates §12.11.5 and calls the *one-sided* form the law: `the law for K is 2K ≤ 2J_c + 2f with the cell's own f`. Main L3432 (§12.11.3.1, read chat 78) and L3038 / L3066 / L3425 all use the one-sided form. MEASURED (r2-ch13b, every cell of Λ₁₂ and Λ₁₃):

| rule | Λ₁₂ kept | Λ₁₂ cut | Λ₁₂ factorisation defect | Λ₁₃ kept | Λ₁₃ cut | Λ₁₃ defect |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| one-sided 2K ≤ 2J_c + 2f | 55,755 | **15,150** | **15,150** | 153,680 | **45,450** | **45,450** |
| two-sided step 2 (MC L1696) | 22,275 | 48,630 | 13,410 | 64,290 | 134,840 | 37,695 |

The printed 15,150 / 45,450 are the one-sided form's, and under that form the cut and the factorisation defect coincide exactly (the tight cells remove no (A-tuple, q) or (B-tuple, q) combination, so Σ_q |A(q)|·|B(q)| stays at the untightened 70,905 / 199,130 — which is why "of the product" is a correct denominator: 15,150/70,905 = 21.3666 %, 45,450/199,130 = 22.8243 %, printed 21.4 % and 22.8 %). Under the MC's exact rule neither figure is the defect. The structural claim survives both readings — either two-parent rule bridges the A and B sides — but the sentence names the rule only as "bounded by J_c … and f", which both satisfy. For R3: name the form at L3475 (and reconcile MC L1264's "the law" with MC L1696's "exact"). No withdrawal; every printed figure in the sentence is exact for the form it was measured on.

**13b-02 · L3466 — "1.887" is Λ₁₁'s mean transfer, printed as the tower's endpoint. (Settles 12c-01 at this site.)** PRINTED L3463–3466: `sections 815 · 3,260 · 6,150 · 3,360 at Λ₁₁, 11,470 · 45,880 · 89,700 · 52,080 at Λ₁₃ … The mean transfer rises, ⟨q⟩ = 1.4631 → 1.887`. MEASURED (r2-ch13b, exact fractions on all cells of every stage): ⟨q⟩ = 357/244 = **1.4631** at Λ₈, 2,787/1,654 = 1.6850 at Λ₉, 928/507 = 1.8304 at Λ₁₀, 5,128/2,717 = **1.8874** at Λ₁₁, 312/163 = 1.9141 at Λ₁₂, 38,152/19,913 = **1.9159** at Λ₁₃. The sentence's own Λ₁₃ sections give 1.9159; 1.887 is Λ₁₁'s. The same figure at the same wrong stage is at Figure 12.3's caption L2431–2432 (`Λ₁₃ solid against Λ₈ dotted … the tower shifts ⟨q⟩ from 1.463 to 1.887`, recorded as 12c-01 in chat 71). No Register entry carries ⟨q⟩ at any stage (grep `1.887` → Register L4725 only, entry 1263, an unrelated quantum defect δ = 1.887). Two sites, one correction, for R3.

## B — verified

- **L3463–3464 the sections.** Λ₁₁ **815 · 3,260 · 6,150 · 3,360** and Λ₁₃ **11,470 · 45,880 · 89,700 · 52,080** reproduce exactly (r2-ch13b, all cells; they sum to 13,585 and 199,130). The section is |A(q)|·|B(q)| with A = (n, ℓ, k, 2S, 2J_c, 2K, 2J) and B = (e, f, g, 2S′, v) per §12.7.1's tower amendment L2406–2408.
- **L3463 "factorises exactly over the transfer … zero defect at every stage."** Σ_q |A(q)|·|B(q)| − |Λ| = **0** at all six stages. The marginals: |A(q)| = 33,33,23,8 (Λ₈–Λ₁₀) → 163,163,123,48 (Λ₁₁) → 819,819,639,264 (Λ₁₂) → 2294,2294,1794,744 (Λ₁₃); |B(q)| = 5,10,15,17 (Λ₈) → 5,15,30,38 (Λ₉) → 5,20,50,70 (Λ₁₀–Λ₁₃).
- **L3464 "log-concave, unimodal, peak at q = 2."** True at every one of the six stages (f(q)² ≥ f(q−1)f(q+1) throughout; argmax = 2 at each).
- **L3465–3466 "the object is still a cylinder — because every coupling axis hangs off one side of the tree."** MEASURED bridge census over the built tower's dependency edges: **no edge crosses the A and B sides**; the only edges at the base are k–q and q–g. Every coupling axis is one-sided: 2S′ (parents g) and v (parents g, 2S′) on B; 2J_c (parent k), 2K (parent 2J_c) and 2J (parent 2K) on A. (This is the §12.11.5 site of 12i-02; the substance is measured true here.)
- **L3475–3476 "the first bridge between the cylinder's two ends other than q."** MEASURED: at every stage of introduction the new axis's bounding parents lie on one side only; the tight 2K ≤ 2J_c + 2f is the first rule with parents on both (2J_c on A, f on B). No earlier cross edge exists to contradict "first".
- **L3477 the percentages.** 15,150/70,905 = 21.3666 % and 45,450/199,130 = 22.8243 % — printed 21.4 % and 22.8 %, correct to the printed precision, with "the product" = Σ_q |A(q)|·|B(q)| = the untightened stage count (see 13b-01).
- **Figure 12.5 caption L3471–3473** — `The parent side thins toward q = 3 while the target side thickens — §12.8.1's trade, seen as shape, at both scales of the tower.` MEASURED: A is monotone non-increasing and B monotone increasing in q at **every** stage, so the claim holds at both the Λ₈ and Λ₁₃ scales the caption draws. The §12.8.1 pointer resolves to heading (L2423) **and** claim (L2424 `\|A_q\| falls 33, 33, 23, 8 while \|B_q\| rises 5, 10, 15, 17`; L2426 `Raising the transfer costs the parent and pays the target, monotonically, and no q improves both`).
- **§12.11.4 L3458–3460.** Not re-derived here: the 12 of 12 (2J_c, f) recoupling identity, 64.4 % through K, 39.4 % direct and the 25 points are measured and banked in `r2-ch12s.out` (READ-ch12s.md B; DEFERRED, chat 76 — read the prose only). The prose was read in full; the two figures' other sites were checked for a naming collision and there is none: 64.4 % at L3038, L3085, L3131 and L3140 is the same axis-13 density throughout.
- **MC L1264 "39,375 of Λ₁₂'s 70,905 cells sit at an f below the cap."** MEASURED 39,375. (For the MC pass; anchored here.)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# r2-ch13b.py — Phase R2, chat 79, segment 1: main §12.11.4 (L3457-3461) and §12.11.5 (L3462-3481).
# Re-measures on ALL cells of every stage: the q-sections |A(q)|, |B(q)|, the fibre |L(q)|, the
# factorisation defect sum_q |A(q)||B(q)| - |L|, log-concavity/unimodality/peak, the mean transfer
# <q>, the Pareto direction of A and B (Figure 12.5 caption), the A/B bridge census (L3466), and the
# tight two-parent K at L12/L13 (count cut, factorisation defect, and both denominators for the
# 21.4 % / 22.8 %).  No wall-clock output.
import importlib.util, os
from fractions import Fraction
from collections import defaultdict
H = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
s = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('r2lib', os.path.join(H, 'r2lib.py'))
r2lib = importlib.util.module_from_spec(s); s.loader.exec_module(r2lib)
T = r2lib.load_tower()

# Coordinate order (tower-2.py header): n0 l1 k2 q3 e4 f5 g6 2S7 | 2S'8 v9 2Jc10 2K11 2J12
# Sides per main §12.7.1's tower amendment (L2406-2408): A runs n-l-k-J_c-K-J with 2S pendant;
# B runs e-f-g-v-2S'; the base is q.
NAME = {0:'n',1:'l',2:'k',3:'q',4:'e',5:'f',6:'g',7:'2S',8:"2S'",9:'v',10:'2Jc',11:'2K',12:'2J'}
A_ALL = (0, 1, 2, 7, 10, 11, 12)
B_ALL = (4, 5, 6, 8, 9)
Q = 3

def sections(X, w):
    """Generalises r2lib.factor_q (r2-ch12i, chat 74) from the 9-coordinate layout to width w.
    Returns q -> (|A(q)|, |B(q)|, |L(q)|)."""
    Ai = [i for i in A_ALL if i < w]; Bi = [i for i in B_ALL if i < w]
    A = defaultdict(set); B = defaultdict(set); N = defaultdict(int)
    for c in X:
        A[c[Q]].add(tuple(c[i] for i in Ai)); B[c[Q]].add(tuple(c[i] for i in Bi)); N[c[Q]] += 1
    return {q: (len(A[q]), len(B[q]), N[q]) for q in sorted(N)}

def logconcave(v):
    return all(v[i]*v[i] >= v[i-1]*v[i+1] for i in range(1, len(v)-1))

def unimodal(v):
    i = v.index(max(v))
    return all(v[j] <= v[j+1] for j in range(i)) and all(v[j] >= v[j+1] for j in range(i, len(v)-1))

def monotone(v, up):
    return all((v[i] <= v[i+1]) if up else (v[i] >= v[i+1]) for i in range(len(v)-1))

STAGES = [('L8', T.L8, 8), ('L9', T.L9, 9), ('L10', T.L10, 10),
          ('L11', T.L11, 11), ('L12', T.L12, 12), ('L13', T.L13, 13)]

print('=== A/B sections, defect, <q>, shape — every cell of every stage ===')
print('stage    |L|        |A(q)|                     |B(q)|                     |L(q)|                     defect  <q>       logcc unim peak Afall Brise')
store = {}
for tag, fn, w in STAGES:
    X = fn(); sec = sections(X, w); qs = sorted(sec)
    Av = [sec[q][0] for q in qs]; Bv = [sec[q][1] for q in qs]; Lv = [sec[q][2] for q in qs]
    prod = sum(a*b for a, b in zip(Av, Bv)); defect = prod - len(X)
    mq = Fraction(sum(q*sec[q][2] for q in qs), len(X))
    store[tag] = (len(X), Av, Bv, Lv, defect, mq)
    print('%-8s %-10s %-25s %-25s %-25s %-7s %-9s %-5s %-4s %-4s %-5s %s' % (

        monotone(Av, False), monotone(Bv, True)))

EDGES = [(0,1),(1,2),(2,3),(2,7),(4,5),(5,6),(3,6),(6,8),(6,9),(8,9),(2,10),(10,11),(11,12)]
